payload.executive_summary: Candidate B2B selects architecture option O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with deterministic integration) and implements it via a four-phase hybrid milestone strategy. Phase 1 delivers the foundational big-bang: Global Orchestrator, Intake & DAG Work Planner, Workspace Manager with namespaced partitions, and a single-lane execution path that validates intake, workspace governance, and the audit spine—effectively proving the O1-equivalent sequential path first. Phase 2 adds the Task Lane Orchestrator and per-lane Writer/Validator/Reviewer/Patcher pods running two parallel lanes on a test repository. Phase 3 introduces the Integration Merge Engine, Integration Validator/Reviewer/Patcher, and the deterministic merge-ordering algorithm that resolves alignment warning AL006. Phase 4 completes the system with the Judge Pod, Freeze Assembler, and full closure gates. This incremental approach de-risks parallelism by proving the single-lane path before adding concurrency, directly addresses the elevated K12 (merge conflicts) and K8 (workspace integrity) risks through phased mitigation, and retains high HITL strictness throughout due to the complexity of parallel execution and unresolved open questions Q7–Q9. The candidate is recommended when wall-clock throughput is a priority and the target repository has low inter-module coupling.

architecture_choice.rationale: O2 is selected because it addresses the primary weakness of O1 (wall-clock time for repos with many independent tasks) while preserving all MUST requirements. The hybrid milestone strategy mitigates O2's higher orchestration complexity by first proving the single-lane sequential path (Phase 1), then incrementally layering parallelism (Phase 2) and deterministic integration (Phase 3). O2's lane-scoped context packs reduce per-invocation context-window pressure (mitigating K9). The namespaced workspace partitions (C22) provide stronger isolation than a single workspace, directly addressing K8. The dedicated Integration Merge Engine (C18) and Integration Validator/Reviewer/Patcher (C19–C21) provide a governed integration sub-flow that addresses K12 and alignment warning AL006 (merge ordering determinism). O1 was rejected as the primary architecture because serialized execution is too slow for repos with many independent modules. O3 was rejected because its per-task micro-cycle model, while excellent for long-horizon resumability, does not provide the parallelism benefit that is the primary driver for this branch. O4 was rejected due to low modularity and risk of undermining CNS12 role separation internally.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json → C12 (Intake & DAG Work Planner): validates inputs, initializes run_manifest/event_log/workspace_index, produces work_plan.json with DAG and lane partitioning → C11 (Global Orchestrator) fans out to C13 (Task Lane Orchestrators): each lane runs C14 (Writer) → C15 (Validator) → C16 (Reviewer) → C17 (Patcher) cycles within lane-scoped workspace partitions managed by C22 → lane completion signals flow back to C11 → C18 (Integration Merge Engine) applies lane patchsets in deterministic order to base repo state, emits conflict reports → C19 (Integration Validator) runs full-repo validation → C20 (Integration Reviewer) produces integration findings → C21 (Integration Patcher) repairs integration issues → C11 routes integrated outputs to C23 (Judge Pod) which produces trace_report and freeze recommendation → C24 (Freeze Assembler) collects all CNS10-required artifacts, runs final closure gates, emits Implementation Freeze Bundle.
key_design_decisions: Phase 1 proves the single-lane sequential path (O1-equivalent) before adding parallelism, de-risking the core intake/workspace/audit infrastructure.
Deterministic merge ordering in C18 is independent of wall-clock lane completion timing, ensuring reproducibility (addresses AL006 and K12).
Namespaced workspace partitions (C22) enforce per-lane isolation with a shared canonical integration partition, mitigating K8.
Per-lane orchestrators (C13) enforce lane-scoped tool permissions and file-path scoping, reducing cross-contamination risk.
High HITL strictness is retained across all phases due to parallel complexity and blocking open questions Q7–Q9.
Integration sub-flow (C18–C21) is a dedicated governed stage with its own validation, review, and patch cycle, not a simple merge step.
Context packs are lane-scoped during parallel execution and integration-scoped during the integration sub-flow, keeping pack sizes bounded (mitigating K9).

milestones.name: Phase 1: Foundation (Big-Bang Single-Lane)

deliverables.text: Global Orchestrator (C11) with DAG workflow engine, budget/retry enforcement, and checkpoint logic.
Intake & DAG Work Planner (C12) with input validation (plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json), run_manifest/event_log initialization, and work_plan.json generation.
Workspace Manager (C22) with namespaced partitions, canonical/non-canonical separation, workspace_index.json maintenance, and checkpoint/restore support.
Single-lane execution path: one Writer (C14), one Validator (C15), one Reviewer (C16), one Patcher (C17) operating sequentially under C11 orchestration.
Audit spine: immutable run_manifest, append-only event_log, versioned artifact store with stage-boundary checkpoints.
Stage_handoff artifacts emitted at every stage transition with required resumable-state fields.
Tool permission matrix enforcement for Intake, WorkPlanning, Generate, PatchApply, Validate, and Review stages.
Secrets detection/redaction/blocking guardrails validated at each checkpoint.

exit_criteria: AT1 passes: valid plan accepted; chat logs and non-canonical inputs rejected.
AT2 passes: missing/invalid repo_context.json rejected; valid repo_context.json accepted.
AT3 passes: missing/invalid workspace_context.json rejected; valid workspace_context.json accepted.
AT4 passes (single-lane subset): stage sequence Intake→Generate→Validate→Review→Patch recorded with checkpoint at each transition.
AT5 passes: stage_handoff artifact present for every stage transition.
AT8 passes: run_manifest immutable; event_log append-only; artifacts versioned and checkpointed.
AT9 passes: prose/markdown artifacts rejected; JSON-only schema-valid artifacts accepted.
AT19 passes: unauthorized tool invocations blocked and logged; authorized invocations succeed.
AT20 passes: secrets detected and blocked/redacted before persistence.

milestones.name: Phase 2: Parallel Lanes (Thin-Slice)

deliverables.text: Task Lane Orchestrator (C13) managing per-lane state machines (Generate→Validate→Review→Patch) with per-lane stage_handoffs and completion signals.
Multi-lane Writer Pool (C14) producing lane-scoped diff-only patchset artifacts.
Per-Lane Validator (C15), Reviewer (C16), and Patcher (C17) pods with lane-scoped context packs.
Per-lane workspace partitions enforced by C22 with lane-scoped tool permissions and file-path scoping.
Demonstration of two parallel lanes executing on a test repository with independent modules.
Per-lane role separation enforcement: writer/reviewer/patcher output-type allowlists per lane.

exit_criteria: AT12 passes: canonical JSON artifact modification via RFC 6902 JSON Patch only; direct replacement rejected.
AT13 passes: diff-only patchset artifacts accepted; non-diff mechanisms rejected.
AT14 passes: forbidden/protected path writes blocked; operation caps enforced.
AT22 passes: writer/reviewer/judge roles distinct per lane; reviewers emit findings-only; multi-vendor routing recorded.

milestones.name: Phase 3: Integration Sub-Flow (Thin-Slice)

deliverables.text: Integration Merge Engine (C18) with deterministic merge ordering algorithm independent of wall-clock lane completion timing.
Integration Validator (C19) running full-repo validators on merged state with integrated test_results.json and quality_reports.json.
Integration Reviewer (C20) producing integration review_findings.json (findings-only).
Integration Patcher (C21) producing integration-level repairs within op caps and escalation thresholds.
Structured conflict_report and integration_report artifacts with deterministic escalation paths.
ChangeRequest artifact schema and deterministic rules for conflict escalation.

exit_criteria: AT15 passes: smallest passing repair selected using deterministic tie-breakers (fewest ops → fewest bytes → first-generated).
AT10 passes: all evidence pointers across integration artifacts use RFC 6901 format and resolve correctly.
AT16 passes: unapproved semantic changes rejected; ChangeRequest with decision record and escalation required.
Deterministic merge ordering produces identical results regardless of lane completion order (integration-specific acceptance criterion from branch strategy).

milestones.name: Phase 4: Judge, Freeze & Full Closure

deliverables.text: Judge Pod (C23) evaluating integrated outputs, producing trace_report.json and freeze/no-freeze recommendation with risk closure assessment against K# entries.
Freeze Assembler (C24) collecting all CNS10-required artifacts, running final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks, emitting decision_record.json and release_bundle.json.
Complete Implementation Freeze Bundle with all required artifacts and directories.
Full closure gate suite: build/test/lint/typecheck, artifact integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, and trace completeness validators.
End-to-end AT# trace mapping in test_results.json for automated trace completeness validation.

exit_criteria: AT5 passes (full run): stage_handoff for every transition including Judge and Freeze boundaries.
AT6 passes: every stage_handoff contains objectives, completed work refs, pending blockers, next actions, and valid evidence pointers.
AT7 passes: freeze bundle contains all minimum required artifacts and directories.
AT17 passes: workspace canonical/non-canonical partition enforced; canonical immutable after freeze; context packs deterministic with evidence pointers.
AT18 passes: all workspace items indexed; no unindexed items or out-of-bounds context packs.
AT21 passes: freeze denied when any gate fails; permitted only when all gates pass.
AT23 passes: flaky retries follow deterministic policy with bounded budgets; exceeded budgets trigger quarantine and escalation.
Full AT suite (AT1–AT23) passes at final Freeze.

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be selected for this candidate?
decision_log.choice: O2 — Task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with deterministic integration sub-flow.
decision_log.rationale: O2 provides wall-clock throughput improvement via parallel lanes while preserving all MUST requirements. The hybrid milestone strategy de-risks by proving the sequential path first (Phase 1). O2's lane-scoped context packs and namespaced workspace partitions address K9 and K8 respectively. The dedicated integration sub-flow addresses K12 and AL006.
alternatives_considered: O1: Sequential staged pipeline — rejected due to slowest wall-clock time for repos with many independent tasks.
O3: Checkpoint-driven micro-cycle — rejected because it lacks parallelism, the primary driver for this branch.
O4: Monolithic council — rejected due to low modularity and risk of undermining CNS12 role separation.
what_would_change_this_decision: Target repository has very high inter-module coupling making lane partitioning infeasible (would favor O1 or O3).
Wall-clock throughput is not a priority and simplicity is paramount (would favor O1).
Long-horizon budget constraints dominate and partial-freeze is critical (would favor O3).

evidence_pointers.note: O2 definition with components C11-C24, interfaces IF10-IF22, and tradeoffs.
Branch B2 rationale selecting O2 for wall-clock throughput priority.

decision_log.question: What milestone strategy should be used to implement O2?
decision_log.choice: Hybrid four-phase strategy: Phase 1 big-bang foundation with single-lane, Phase 2 thin-slice parallel lanes, Phase 3 thin-slice integration, Phase 4 judge/freeze/closure.
decision_log.rationale: The hybrid approach de-risks by first proving the single-lane sequential path works (Phase 1), then incrementally adding parallelism (Phase 2) and integration (Phase 3). This ensures the foundational infrastructure (intake, workspace governance, audit spine) is validated before introducing the complexity of parallel execution and merge ordering.
alternatives_considered: Pure thin-slice from the start — rejected because parallel infrastructure depends on foundational components being proven first.
Two-phase approach (foundation + everything else) — rejected because integration sub-flow complexity warrants its own phase for focused validation.
what_would_change_this_decision: Team has prior experience with parallel orchestration infrastructure, reducing Phase 1 validation need.
Time pressure requires collapsing phases 2 and 3.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B2 milestone strategy specifying hybrid four-phase approach.

decision_log.question: How should merge ordering determinism be guaranteed in the integration sub-flow?
decision_log.choice: C18 (Integration Merge Engine) applies lane patchsets in a deterministic order defined by work_plan.json task DAG topology, independent of wall-clock lane completion timing. Conflicts exceeding automated resolution thresholds trigger structured escalation (reroute to integration patcher or HITL).
decision_log.rationale: Deterministic ordering independent of completion timing is required for reproducibility (alignment warning AL006). The work_plan DAG provides a stable, auditable ordering basis. Escalation thresholds prevent unbounded automated conflict resolution.
alternatives_considered: Completion-order-based merge — rejected because it introduces wall-clock nondeterminism.
Alphabetical file-path ordering — rejected because it ignores logical dependency structure.
what_would_change_this_decision: Open question Q9 is resolved with a different conflict resolution strategy.
Work_plan DAG proves insufficient for ordering (e.g., many independent tasks with no topological order) — would need supplemental deterministic tie-breaker.

evidence_pointers.note: C18 Integration Merge Engine responsibilities including deterministic merge ordering.
K12 merge conflict risk and mitigation requiring deterministic ordering independent of wall-clock timing.
AL006 alignment warning on merge ordering determinism.

decision_log.question: What governance posture should be applied for tooling and HITL?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed tooling with high HITL strictness across all phases.
decision_log.rationale: Parallel execution introduces elevated risks (K12 merge conflicts, K8 workspace integrity, K10 role separation across lanes). High HITL strictness ensures human oversight at critical junctures. Sandboxed tooling enforces deny-by-default tool permissions per the tool policy matrix. Open questions Q7–Q9 remain blocking, further justifying conservative governance.
alternatives_considered: Medium HITL strictness — rejected due to unresolved open questions and elevated parallel-execution risks.
Unsandboxed tooling — rejected as it violates CNS1 and tool permission matrix requirements.
what_would_change_this_decision: Open questions Q7–Q9 are resolved, reducing uncertainty about diff format, repair selection, and conflict resolution.
Demonstrated track record of safe parallel execution in similar repos.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B2 governance posture: sandboxed tooling, high HITL strictness.
HITL policy with interruption triggers and approval roles.

decision_log.question: Which acceptance tests gate which milestone phases?
decision_log.choice: Phase 1: AT1-AT3, AT4 (single-lane subset), AT5, AT8, AT9, AT19, AT20. Phase 2: AT12, AT13, AT14, AT22. Phase 3: AT15, AT10, AT16 plus integration-specific merge ordering criterion. Phase 4: AT5-AT7, AT17, AT18, AT21, AT23 plus full AT suite at final Freeze.
decision_log.rationale: Tests are allocated to the earliest phase where the corresponding functionality is delivered. Phase 1 validates foundational infrastructure. Phase 2 validates per-lane mechanics. Phase 3 validates integration and change control. Phase 4 validates end-to-end closure. Full AT suite runs at final Freeze for comprehensive regression coverage.
alternatives_considered: Running full AT suite at every phase — rejected as premature tests would fail on undelivered functionality.
Deferring all testing to Phase 4 — rejected as it eliminates incremental validation benefit of phased delivery.
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement priorities change, shifting functionality between phases.
New acceptance tests are added that map to specific phase deliverables.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B2 acceptance strategy mapping ATs to phases.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Elevated Risk Assessment for Parallel Execution
supplemental_evaluations.notes: O2 elevates several risks compared to O1: K12 (merge conflicts) becomes the primary risk due to parallel lane patchsets potentially overlapping; mitigated by Phase 3's deterministic merge ordering and explicit conflict escalation. K8 (workspace integrity) risk increases with namespaced partitions; mitigated by C22 partition enforcement and workspace integrity validators at each checkpoint. K10 (role separation) risk increases with parallel pods; mitigated by per-lane orchestrator-enforced output-type allowlists. K9 (context pack overflow) risk is actually lower per-lane due to smaller scoped packs but integration-stage packs may be larger. K6 (flaky tests) risk is distributed across lanes but integration revalidation can amplify it. All mitigations are addressed in specific milestone phases.

evidence.note: K12 merge conflict risk — primary elevated risk for O2.
K8 workspace integrity risk — elevated due to namespaced partitions.
K10 role separation risk — elevated with parallel pods.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Blocking Open Questions Impact on B2B
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Open questions Q7 (diff format), Q8 (smallest passing repair selection), and Q9 (conflict resolution for parallel patchsets) are all blocking and directly impact O2's parallel execution model. Q7 affects patchset format across all lanes and integration. Q8 affects repair selection in both per-lane and integration patch cycles. Q9 is the most critical for O2 specifically, as it determines how C18 handles overlapping lane outputs. The high HITL strictness posture and Phase 3's dedicated integration focus are designed to accommodate resolution of these questions. Until Q7-Q9 are resolved, Phase 3 implementation details remain provisional.

evidence.note: Q8 — smallest passing repair selection blocking question.
Q9 — conflict resolution for parallel patchsets blocking question.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Pruning Guidance
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Candidate B2B (O2 parallel lanes) is recommended when: (1) wall-clock throughput is a priority, (2) the target repository has low inter-module coupling enabling clean lane partitioning, and (3) the team is prepared for the higher orchestration complexity. It should be pruned in favor of B1 (O1 sequential) when the repo has high inter-module coupling or simplicity is paramount, or in favor of O3 when long-horizon partial-freeze resumability is the dominant concern.

evidence.note: Branch B2 rationale and pruning hints.
